articles.title: Shipwreck Hunters Discover the Ruins of a British Destroyer That Split in Half During a Tragic Peacetime Accident 118 Years Ago
articles.summary: In 1908, Royal Navy ships, including HMS Tiger, conducted a training exercise involving Whitehead torpedo tubes during a moonless night in the English Channel. This historical event highlights early 20th-century naval drills and the technological advancements in maritime warfare. Understanding such historical operations provides valuable context for the evolution of modern defence strategies and naval readiness.

articles.title: Your Android phone is mangling lossless audio before it even reaches your headphones
articles.summary: Android devices may inadvertently degrade audio quality, even for hi-res files, due to their internal audio mixer, AudioFlinger. This system component resamples almost all audio content, potentially lowering the sound fidelity without the user's knowledge. Aspirants should be aware of such technical limitations that can impact their media experience on Android platforms.

articles.title: Lanterns Shines Bright With 9.3M Views In First 3 Days On HBO Max - Biggest Launch For A DC Studios Show
articles.summary: The new DCU series 'Lanterns' has launched successfully on HBO and HBO Max, achieving 9.3 million views in its first three days. This strong debut marks the biggest premiere for any DC series on these platforms, demonstrating significant global audience engagement. The success underscores the continued international appeal of the DC Universe in digital entertainment.

articles.title: DC 'People v. Gorilla Grodd' Set at HBO Max Skyler Gisondo Jimmy Tatro
articles.summary: HBO Max is moving forward with its DC Studios mockumentary series, "The People v. Gorilla Grodd." First reported in November 2025, this production will likely offer a satirical look at the legal and societal implications surrounding the highly intelligent, telepathic ape villain from the DC universe, blending fictional science with mockumentary storytelling.

articles.title: India's forgotten gourmet produce: Tellicherry pepper, Lakadong turmeric, and Kashmiri morels
articles.summary: Monsoon winds, a seasonal phenomenon bringing moisture to India, were historically crucial for trade. Millennia ago, ancient traders skillfully utilized these powerful winds to sail ships filled with valuable goods like gold and silver to India, highlighting the region's historical economic significance and sophisticated early maritime connections driven by natural elements.

articles.title: The long and winding R&D: While India tracks where publicly funded research money goes, it should track what it creates
articles.summary: India's research-funding ecosystem is estimated to be losing over ₹3,000 crore annually due to duplicate grants. This significant financial drain, comparable to issues highlighted by a US analysis, indicates a critical inefficiency in resource allocation for scientific advancement. For SSB aspirants, this underlines the importance of robust financial oversight and transparent management in national institutions to ensure optimal utilization of public funds for development.

articles.title: Too young to ask their own questions: Learning and visitor dynamics in a constructivist museum environment
articles.summary: The National Museum in Prague launched a new permanent Childrens Museum exhibition in 2023. Primarily for ages 5-10, it aims to offer an engaging and educational experience. This initiative reflects efforts to make national cultural institutions more accessible and appealing to younger audiences, fostering early learning and interaction with history and culture, highlighting cultural development in other nations.
